Do you get excited by the shape of a whole world: the districts, the landmarks, the routes between them, and the little details that make a place feel lived in? Then you might be exactly who we're looking for.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're growing! Triband is working on our most ambitious project to date: a new systemic open-world game built around a beloved IP, with our own spin on it. A bold new direction for us! And we're just getting started. Now we're looking for a Senior World Designer to plan, prototype, and build this world. You'll shape the big picture (the areas, how they connect, and how players find their way around) and work hands-on in the engine to bring it to life together with artists, designers, and the rest of your team. If maps and dots and their connections make you happy, you’ll probably like what comes next.

**Here's What You'll Do Day To Day

**

• Plan the world and lead its conceptualization, keeping a clear overview and vision for the whole map and for each new area before we start building it

• Create distinct spaces, biomes, and sections of the world (grounded in the real world), working closely with the art team to make each one feel unique

• Collaborate with artists and your team on environmental storytelling that gives each region its own identity

• Design how players navigate the world, using landmarks and the systems behind them

• Establish and maintain the world-creation pipeline, workflows, and hierarchy structures

• Work with developers on the tools that help build the world, such as traffic networks

• Gather needs from across the team and make sure they land in the right places in the world

• Build and implement hands-on in the engine like the rest of the team

**You're a great match if

**

• You have extensive in-engine experience. We use Unity, so that's preferred, but experience with other engines works too

• You've worked as a world or level designer on an open-world game as part of a team, and you know the common pitfalls of open-world design

• You have a strong macro-level design approach, balancing ideas and needs from different team members to create spaces that are believable, navigable, and fun

• You have experience establishing and maintaining detailed world and content documentation, and you like maps and spreadsheets

• A tidy hierarchy makes you happy, and you keep the small details and the big picture in view at the same time

• “Let’s try it out” is your favorite way to solve a problem

• You iterate on your work and stay open to changing it as the project evolves

• Balancing the needs of artists, designers, and programmers is a puzzle you enjoy rather than a chore

**Nice to have

**

• You enjoy building moment-to-moment, concrete level design too

• You can make people see a space before it exists, through a mood board, a rough walkthrough, or the story of a player’s first hour there

• You have an interest in urban planning and/or architecture

• You keep up with industry norms in open-world games

• You're drawn to casual, family-friendly, quirky universe building and storytelling

• You have experience prototyping mini games and activities

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward.

• You're motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture.

• You believe games are made by teams, not solo rockstars, and that good ideas can come from anyone.

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them.

• You're up for experimentation, and at the same time you don't get too precious when the experience tells you you're wrong.

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place.

**Practicalities

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• This role is based in the Greater Copenhagen area, and we're not offering relocation for this one.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

• Most importantly: no crunch. People over deadlines.

**We offer

**

• A shot at shaping the world of a live game played by millions

• A tight, collaborative team where your ideas actually make it into the game

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, and whatever else Tribanders turn into a tradition

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant, with plant-based options and soft ice on Thursdays

• Pension plan and private health insurance

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Endless amounts of Cocio

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide.

From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make people laugh. We explore comedy through gameplay, which means we like to break player expectations, create surprising interactions, use great music and slick art, and build quirky worlds full of personality.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games. And we believe diversity makes teams better. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and who are excited to challenge us and our way of doing things.

For more info about Triband, check out: triband.net/about

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

We're creating a new role at the top of our Engineering career ladder: Lead Architect. It's the senior end of our Technical Track — the rung above Tech Lead — and today it's a role we've deliberately left lightly defined, because we want the first person in it to help define it. You'll set Factbird's technical direction: architecture, tooling, and the multi-year technology bets that shape where the product goes next.

This is our most senior technical role, with no direct reports — your authority comes from judgment and track record, not the org chart. You'll work alongside our Tech Leads in Factbird's technical leadership group, partner closely with our Director of Engineering, and be the person other senior engineers go to when a decision is genuinely hard to reverse.

About the Role

As Lead Architect, you own Factbird's company-wide technical vision: the architecture our services run on, the tooling and standards our engineers use every day, and the multi-year technology strategy that ties it all together. You make — or sign off on — the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse architecture calls, and you're accountable for getting them right with the full context of where the business is headed, not just where the code is today.

You'll work across a team built on Rust, React, Node.js, and AWS, with AI-assisted development already a core part of how we ship. Some of what this role owns is already well-defined — reviewing RFCs, stewarding language and platform standards, setting the team's AI-tooling strategy. Some of it isn't yet: Factbird is still a growing company, and part of the job is helping us figure out what technical leadership at this level should look like as we scale.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be trusted with genuinely hard calls than manage a team, and if you can hold both the technical detail and the commercial context — cost, risk, market direction — well enough to make a technology bet you can still defend a year later.

What you'll do

Architecture & technical strategy

• Own Factbird's multi-year technology strategy, and make the high-stakes architecture calls that are hard to reverse — with cost, risk, and business context factored in, not just engineering elegance

• Author and drive major RFCs from proposal through to an actual decision, and review the highest-risk architecture changes across the team

• Act as steward for our core languages and frameworks — setting standards, library choices, and the platform's overall shape

• Make build-vs-buy calls for new technical capabilities, and bring a clear point of view on emerging technologies worth adopting

• Define the observability, reliability, and security posture the platform is held to

Tooling & standards

• Set the team's technical tooling and platform standards, and keep them evolving as the stack and the company grow

• Define Factbird's strategy for AI-assisted development — which tools we adopt, how we balance velocity against code quality, security, and IP risk, and where we draw the line

• Shape engineering-wide quality philosophy and help set the technical bar used in hiring interviews

• Help define shared components and reference architecture that other engineers build on, rather than reinvent

• Give input into technical org design and team topology as Engineering scales

Technical leadership & mentorship

• Act as the trusted technical advisor to our Director of Engineering and the technical leadership group, partnering with Tech Leads and Product Leads on cross-team alignment

• Mentor senior engineers and Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without formal ownership of their people management

• Communicate technical vision and trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including leadership

• Identify technical risks to the business early, and say so before they become expensive

• Represent Factbird's technical thinking externally where it makes sense — a talk, a blog post, an open-source contribution — though this isn't a requirement on day one

What we’re looking for

We're looking for someone who's already earned this kind of trust somewhere else — someone whose technical opinions carry weight because they're right more often than not, and who'd rather solve the interesting, ambiguous problem than manage the team solving it.

The ideal background

• 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience, including real time spent as an architect or equivalent senior technical authority, not just a senior engineer with a bigger title

• A track record of owning multi-year technology strategy or platform architecture decisions that other teams had to live with — and that held up

• Has led major RFCs or architecture proposals cross-team, through genuine pushback, to an actual decision

• Comfortable making build-vs-buy and technology-adoption calls that account for cost, risk, and where the market is heading, not just what's technically interesting

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without needing formal authority to do it

• Practical, current experience with AI-assisted development, and a clear point of view on where it genuinely helps versus where it creates risk

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

We'd love to hear from you

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at crva@factbird.com

At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

Build the systems behind our power trading - from real-time data and algorithmic execution to the trading terminal our desk uses every day.

The role

Join a small team that builds and owns our trading platform end to end. Work directly with traders, take responsibility for production systems and see the impact of what you ship.

What you will work on

• Order management, trading algorithms and real-time execution.

• Market data integrations and our trading terminal.

• Scheduling, nominations and reconciliation with TSOs and exchanges.

• Platform reliability, infrastructure and security.

What you bring

At least 3-5 years of experience building and running production systems. You can take an open-ended problem from idea to deployment, communicate clearly and take ownership when things break. Experience with concurrent or real-time systems is valuable; curiosity about power markets is essential.

Our stack

Backend: Kotlin, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB, RabbitMQ, gRPC and websockets.

Frontend: React, TypeScript and D3.

Platform: Docker, Kubernetes, Azure DevOps, Entra ID and OpenTelemetry.

You do not need to know every tool. Be strong in one area and ready to learn the rest.

What we offer

Real ownership, competitive compensation and a small, experienced team. Our office is in central Aarhus, close to the traders and the decisions your work supports.

Interested?

Send a short introduction and your CV. Questions about the role are welcome too.

Apply by email ↗contact@aarhustrading.dk

Sparrow Quantum is seeking an experimental physicist to develop deterministic entanglement sources for photonic quantum computing. You will build and automate experiments on single quantum emitters coupled to photonic nanostructures, taking responsibility for the optical setup, the supporting electronics and the control software, and translate the results into technical direction for device and system development.

Your role

• 
Design, build and operate quantum optics experiments combining integrated photonics, cryogenics and single-photon detection

• 
Take ownership of the software for instrument control, experiment automation and data acquisition, and keep it maintainable, versioned and usable by the rest of the team

• 
Design and build simple electronics and hardware for the lab, such as driver circuits, interface boards, interlocks and mechanical fixtures

• 
Contribute to research activities on photonic quantum computing and share results clearly with the team

• 
Collaborate with academic and industrial partners in national and European projects

Must have

• 
PhD in physics or a closely related field

• 
Hands-on experience in an optics lab, in academia or industry

• 
Strong practical skills in free-space and fibre optics, lasers and spectroscopy

• 
Solid programming skills, ideally in Python, for controlling hardware and automating experiments, and a genuine drive to write good code rather than just enough to get by

• 
Curiosity and the persistence to track down problems and refine the final result

• 
Willingness to collaborate and deliver results in a clear and structured way

• 
Strong focus on the final goal, self-discipline and prioritisation

Nice to have

• 
Experience with Git and GitHub, including code review and collaborative development

• 
Experience with single quantum emitters, such as quantum dots, colour centres, atoms, ions or molecules

• 
Experience with cryostats, single-photon detectors and time-tagging electronics

• 
Familiarity with FPGA or real-time control, electro-optic modulators and fast electronics

• 
Experience with InAs/GaAs quantum dots and integrated quantum photonics, including waveguides, photonic crystals or cavities

• 
Knowledge of quantum information, including multiphoton entanglement, cluster states or photonic quantum computing

• 
A track record of scientific publications

What you can expect

• 
A central role in building the experimental and software infrastructure of a company at the forefront of photonic quantum computing

• 
A high-performance team of highly motivated people working towards photonic quantum computing

• 
Contributing to scientific publications and patents

• 
Competitive salary

• 
Lunches paid by the company

• 
The possibility of travelling to our collaborators for new insights and knowledge sharing

• 
A steep learning curve in a supportive environment at the boundary between research and industry

How to apply

If you share our passion for delivering a real-world impact through the development of unique quantum photonic technology and have the skills we believe are essential for future Sparrows, we would love to hear from you.

We are committed to creating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace at Sparrow Quantum and welcome applicants from all backgrounds and identities.

How to apply: Scroll down to apply with your CV and a short cover letter (in English).

Application deadline: November 23.

Starting date: As soon as possible.

Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis

Short-listed candidates will be invited for an in-person interview in Copenhagen. Travel and accommodation will be covered.

For questions, contact Alexey Tiranov.

About Sparrow Quantum

Sparrow Quantum is a Danish quantum technology company dedicated to advancing light-matter interfaces for quantum technologies. We are recognized globally for our high-performance single-photon sources and our foundational contributions to the quantum internet and quantum computing.

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

Genmab is searching for an energized Senior Associate to be part of Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery team in Copenhagen within commute distance from our office locations to work according to your hybrid work arrangement.

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. During inspections, you will participate in back-office activities and help ensure timely retrieval and follow-up of requested information.

The role also offers opportunities to develop beyond inspection readiness. Working closely with Clinical Supply Managers in the Portfolio & Project Delivery team and colleagues across the department, you will support selected operational tasks and initiatives while gaining broader exposure to clinical trial management. Through collaboration with Clinical Trial Operations and CROs, and hands-on involvement in clinical supply activities, you will further develop your GCP and clinical supply knowledge.

The position is based in Copenhagen.

**Responsibilities

**

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support activities related to day-to-day trial management, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Support distribution and logistics, including tasks related to shipment documentation, in alignment with the Drug Supply Managers.

• Build knowledge of especially GCP but also GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery function

• Participate in maintenance and continuous improvement of procedures, tools and ways of working supporting inspection readiness and clinical supply activities.

• Responsible for being compliant with Genmab´s quality system.

**Requirements

**

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GCP and GMP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GCP/GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functional with internal and external stakeholders.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

**The Team

**You will be part of a highly competent team focused on end-to-end trial management including planning and maintenance of supplies for clinical trials, working closely with cross-functional stakeholders in both CMC and Clinical Trial Operations.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department. We foster a supportive, international, and fast-paced work environment centered on collaboration, excellence, and a can-do attitude to achieve results.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Both Orthodontists and Dentists are an integral part of our doctor driven business. Our goal is to deliver superior clinical outcomes with an enhanced patient experience. Our continued growth and success depends on enabling dental clinics to thrive.

Your mission as a sales Territory Manager is to apply comprehensive knowledge of Invisalign and iTero sales strategies for key accounts to accelerate revenue and higher case volume. You will sell directly to professional business owners (Dentists and Orthodontists), transforming an analog process with clear aligners and innovative digital solutions that make straightening teeth easier, faster, and more accessible – helping practitioners grow their business and increase patient satisfaction.

Role expectations

• Use a consultative selling approach and data-driven insights to educate customers, challenge existing business practices, drive growth, and support the adoption of digital technology and workflow optimization.

• Achieve quarterly and annual territory sales targets and revenue goals.

• Manage a defined geographic territory, grow existing accounts, and identify, onboard, and develop high-potential new accounts.

• Develop and execute territory business plans based on account potential, market opportunities, and growth objectives.

• Create and implement strategic account plans for high-potential customers by assessing business goals, challenges, needs, and growth opportunities.

• Leverage data analytics and business insights to support customer decision-making and drive business performance.

• Educate dental professionals on Invisalign and iTero products, services, and digital solutions to build clinical confidence and support product adoption.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with doctors, treatment coordinators, clinical assistants, education, marketing, and product development teams to understand customer needs and align Align solutions with practice objectives.

• Coordinate internal resources to enhance the customer experience, strengthen relationships, and drive ongoing adoption of Align products, services, and digital solutions.

• Analyze customer needs, identify business opportunities, and recommend tailored solutions that deliver a high-quality customer experience.

• Develop and execute territory and account strategies independently, prioritizing critical tasks with urgency, accountability, and strong organizational skills.

• Engage customers through in-person and virtual sales channels, adapting sales strategies to customer preferences and business needs.

What we're looking for

• Bachelor’s degree and/or equivalent experience required

• Minimum of 4 years of experience required. Experience can be outside business-to-business (B2B) sales experience or industry experience selling a medical device, capital equipment, dental or other relevant combination of sales (inside or outside) and industry experience

• Proven track record of achieving sales goals

• Possess and maintain a valid driver’s license

• Business & Marketing knowledge: Ability & comfort having business discussions (Cash Flow Analysis, ROI, P&L) and asking the right business questions

• Comfort with having clinical discussions regarding both Invisalign and iTero product

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.  Experience with a CRM system, Salesforce preferred, and virtual communication platforms

• Regular travel within assigned geographical territory required with the possibility of some overnight travel required. Some travel to the US will be required

• Legally entitled to work in Canada and travel to the US on occasion

Pay Transparency

For Field Sales roles, the salary listed is the base pay only and does not include the applicable incentive compensation plan. A cost of living adjustment may be added to base pay for higher cost areas in the U.S.

This posting is for an existing vacancy within our organization. Canadian work experience is not required for this position.  We welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

We use automated tools (including artificial intelligence “AI”) in our hiring process. This may include AI-based screening or assessment of applications. All final hiring decisions will be made by humans.

jobs.description:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Ecoscience programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027.

Title:
Optimizing grazing management for biodiversity in semi-natural habitats: evidence from monitoring, remote sensing and field experiments

Research area and project description:
How can grazing management be optimized to benefit both biodiversity and nature-based beef production? This PhD project will address this question through analyses of long-term biodiversity monitoring data, development of digital biodiversity indicators, and field experiments in Danish semi-natural habitats.

Grazing is a key ecological process in many ecosystems. However, biodiversity outcomes depend on how grazing is managed, including grazing intensity and timing. Despite its widespread use as a conservation tool, important knowledge gaps remain regarding which grazing strategies deliver the greatest biodiversity benefits and how these outcomes can be documented in a robust and scalable way.

The PhD project is part of the interdisciplinary Nature&Beef initiative and will combine ecology, biodiversity monitoring, remote sensing and data science. The selected candidate will work with unique datasets from the Danish national biodiversity monitoring programme (NOVANA), field experiments, drone imagery and other digital monitoring approaches.

The project will focus on four interconnected themes:
1) Identifying grazing practices associated with positive biodiversity outcomes using long-term monitoring data.
2) Evaluating the effects of grazing intensity and grazing season on biodiversity in a large-scale field experiment.
3) Developing and validating image-based indicators of vegetation structure and biodiversity condition from field and drone imagery.
4) Contributing to the development of AI-based methods for mapping vegetation and habitat condition from drone images.

The project offers an opportunity to contribute to evidence-based conservation and the development of practical tools that can support land managers, farmers, conservation practitioners and value-chain actors in documenting biodiversity outcomes. The findings will help build a stronger scientific foundation for biodiversity-friendly grazing practices and nature-based beef production.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants to the PhD position must have a Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in biology or equivalent. The applicants have documented experience in botanical surveys including species identification skills of North-European flora. The applicant must have a driver license applicable in Denmark. Demonstrated proficiency in data management and analysis, image analysis, and experience using R.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher(s) in Digital Media, Computational Methods and Democracy
jobs.description:
The Department of Communication and Arts at Roskilde University invites applications for one or two postdoctoral position(s) in a new research project on digital media and the conditions for democratic debate. The position is a full-time appointment for 24 months, starting on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

We welcome candidates with backgrounds in digital methods, computational social science, science and technology studies (STS), sociology, communication studies, political communication, media studies, information studies, digital humanities, or related fields in the humanities and social sciences.

About the project
The postdoc position is associated with an ambitious three-year project funded by the Politiken Foundation (Politiken-Fonden) through its largest ever research initiative, which seeks to investigate how digital technologies are shaping democratic debate. You will be part of a team researching how digital news media, search engines, social media, and AI chatbots present pressing issues in Danish public debate. Our central concern is the scope of public issues as they are represented online, how this varies between platforms and between people's actual online experiences, and how digital media shape the range of perspectives citizens encounter. While much research and public debate focuses on misinformation, disinformation, polarisation and hate speech, another fundamental question is whether digital media expose us to a sufficiently diverse range of actors, arguments, and viewpoints to support a productive democratic conversation. Do digital platforms broaden the range of concerns and perspectives that can enter democratic debate, or do they narrow the ways in which public issues are represented and understood?

The project will answer this by developing two complementary research tools:

• The Democratic Debate Meter: A public-facing digital tool that systematically tracks and compares how selected public issues — such as hybrid warfare, agricultural taxation, health services, or school reform — are represented across digital platforms. Using computational digital methods, including text analysis and simulated searches, we investigate which actors and topics become visible.
• The Live Data Donation Lab: A participatory research initiative that combines data donations with browser-based capture of digital content. Working with citizens, journalists, and policymakers, we investigate how personalised digital environments shape people's encounters with and sensemaking around public issues and involve participants in interpreting findings and developing our analytical approach.
By combining computational analysis with qualitative and participatory methods, the project aims to advance research on digital media and democracy. We are focused on producing publicly accessible findings, reports and tools that contribute to wider debates about the role of digital platforms in democratic life, while also contributing to cutting edge academic research at the highest international level.

The position
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will play a central role in the project's research activities, working closely with the project leaders and other team members. You will contribute to the collection and analysis of digital data, the development of methods for comparing representations of public issues across platforms, and the interpretation and communication of findings. Depending on your background and interests, there will be opportunities to contribute to computational text analysis, methodological development, public-facing data visualizations, qualitative research, participatory workshops and public dissemination. You will also contribute to the project's research publications and its public-facing outputs, including the Debate Meter and reports on the scope of issue representation across digital media.

The position offers an opportunity to develop an independent research profile while collaborating on a bold interdisciplinary project that connects methodological innovation with an important question for contemporary democracy. You will be part of an enthusiastic and supportive research environment at Roskilde University, with opportunities to participate in international conferences, workshops and research collaborations. In recent years, faculty have enjoyed a highly successful record of obtaining research grants for large national and international projects broadly focused on questions around digitalisation and democracy, meaning you will be joining a department where young and senior scholars are actively collaborating on a number of ambitious research initiatives in these areas.

The position is based at the Department of Communication and Arts, with affiliation to the Centre for Digital Citizenship and the Digital Media Lab. You will work closely with the project leader, Associate Professor Andreas Birkbak, and the co-investigator Professor Chris Peters.

Qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who is curious about how digital technologies shape public debate and who is interested in developing innovative ways to study these processes. Applicants must hold a PhD, or expect to obtain one by the time of appointment, in a relevant field within social science, the humanities, or data science.We are particularly interested in candidates who bring some combination of the following:

• Computational and digital methods: Experience with, or a strong interest in developing, computational approaches to digital data, especially text analysis and digital trace data and the comparative analysis of online content. Experience with qualitative, participatory or interpretive methods is also an advantage.
• Research on media and democracy: An interest in how digital media shape public debate, democratic participation and the visibility of different actors, issues and perspectives.
• Theoretical and methodological breadth: Familiarity with relevant approaches in STS, digital methods, media and communication studies, platform studies, controversy mapping, or related fields.
• Research communication: An interest in communicating research beyond academia, including through public reports, digital visualisations, workshops, or engagement with journalists and other societal actors.
• Good command of Danish is essential, as the project analyses Danish-language media content and public debate. Good command of English is also required, including the ability to write and publish research in English.
We do not expect candidates to be equally experienced in all these areas. We welcome applicants with complementary profiles who can contribute their own expertise while developing new skills through collaboration with the project team.

Responsibilities
The successful candidate(s) will be expected to:

• Contribute actively to the design and implementation of the project's research activities.
• Collect, process and analyse digital media data, including contributing to computational text analysis.
• Develop and apply analytical methods, in dialogue with the project's theoretical and empirical concerns.
• Contribute to research publications, both independently and in collaboration with the project team.
• Help communicate research to wider audiences through reports, digital outputs and other activities.
• Participate in workshops, conferences and collaborations with academic and non-academic partners.
• Contribute to the department's collegial and interdisciplinary research environment.
Assessment
In assessing applicants, particular consideration will be given to:

• The relevance and quality of the applicant's research experience and publications
• Potential for contributing to computational and digital methods and methodological innovation.
• The applicant's established theoretical and empirical interests on digital media and democracy.
• Experience with interdisciplinary collaboration and communicating research to wider audiences.
• Potential to contribute to the project and to the wider research environment at Roskilde University.
Further information
For further information about the position or the project, please contact the project leader Associate Professor Andreas Birkbak, at andreasbi@ruc.dk or +45 28 79 93 16. We expect job interviews to be held in February 2027.
